messages:
nina: Quick sync — thinking through per-route analytics bookmarks (saved views) + who owns them. We keep hearing that product teams want route-specific defaults, but platform wants org-level canonical views. Can we align?

sam: +1 that it's been a pain. Most PMs just want a "default" dashboard when they open a route. They don't care about global views unless it's shared across product lines.

tom: Technical constraint: our current saved-query model only has `scope: org|user`. Adding `route` or `model` scope is straightforward but we need to update the router and permission checks. Also affects telemetry explorer and console caching.

ali: Important to remember quotas/visibility: route-scoped saved views should inherit route-level read perms. If a route is private in a team space, org-level views shouldn't leak.

kevin: From sales/PS, customers repeatedly ask for "per-route pinning" so engineers landing on a route see the team's curated metrics. Also they'd like a way to mark a view as "official" so SREs don't override it during incidents.

sam: UX idea: allow pinning a saved view to a route with metadata: pinned_by, pinned_at, pinned_scope (team/org). Pin shows at top of route analytics. Non-pinned saved views live under "Shared views".

nina: Questions: (1) default scope for new saved view created from route UI? (2) what API changes do we need? (3) migration for existing org-level saved queries?

tom: For (1) I propose default = "route" if created from a route page, fallback to "org" if created from global analytics. For programmatic saves via API, require scope param.

ali: That default makes sense from security perspective. Also add an explicit confirmation modal when saving to org scope that calls out visibility.

sam: UX followups: add a small badge on the saved view card: "Route" / "Org" / "Personal" and a 3-dot menu to change scope (if you have perms).

kevin: For "official" designation: only org admins or route owners can mark a view as canonical. That should be a flag on the saved view metadata.

tom: API sketch (console internal API). We'll need a new field on saved views: `scope: "user" | "route" | "org"`, plus `route_id` nullable when scope=="route", `owned_by` (team id or user id), and `canonical: boolean`. Example payload (POST /api/saved_views):
```json
{
  "name": "P50 / token cost - HTTP / route",
  "query": "group_by=route&metric=p50_latency",
  "scope": "route",
  "route_id": "route_1234",
  "owned_by": "team_platform",
  "canonical": false
}
```

sam: Nice. Also we should include `pinned: boolean` and `pinned_by` / `pinned_at` when pinned.

ali: Implementation notes: router needs to resolve view when loading /routes/:id/analytics. Priority: pinned route canonical view -> canonical route view -> team-owned route view -> user pinned -> org default. We must document fallback order and caching TTLs.

nina: Migration: existing org-level saved views created from route pages — do we retroactively convert those to `route` scope? Risky. Maybe leave them as `org` but allow route owners to "adopt" an org view into route scope (copy + owned_by set).

tom: Agree. Migration plan: list all saved_views with a link to a route in their query, then surface them in a migration UI where owners can adopt or leave as org. We'll add an audit log entry for adoption.

kevin: Buyers asked for an audit trail — please include `created_by`, `created_at`, `last_modified_by`. That helps when PS sets canonical views during onboarding.

ali: We should also consider quotas — how many saved views per org/route? Probably default 100/org and 20/route, configurable via account plan. Avoid unbounded explosion.

sam: Small UX ask: quick keyboard shortcut to switch between "route views" and "org views" and a pin icon on the top bar. :keyboard: :pushpin:

nina: Next steps: tom/ali to draft the API schema and permission checks by EOD Friday. sam/kevin to prototype the UI copy and migration modal. I'll schedule a 30m sync Tue to review.

deploy-bot: "deploy queued: feature/saved-views-route-scope" — CI passed :white_check_mark:

tom: One more thing — need to update telemetry so per-route default views count as "view loads" for billing/usage. We'll add a flag `is_default_view_load` to events so Optimize and billing can use it.

nina: Great — logging that. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
